facts.text: St. Pierre grew from 1888 encampments of Cree refugees and landless Chippewa who fled treaties, forming the community that now sits on former Fort Assiniboine.
St. Pierre sits on the northwestern edge of the Bears Paw Mountains, in southeastern Hill County.
The community celebrates Chippewa Cree heritage each year with the Rocky Boy's Pow Wow, drawing visitors from across the reservation.
St. Pierre’s economy relies on tribal government services, agriculture, livestock, and modest natural resource projects, with jobs from the Bureau of Indian Affairs and local schools.
The town’s site was chosen after Indian Affairs investigated and recommended settling landless Chippewa Cree at the abandoned Fort Assiniboine in the Bear Paw Mountains.
About 88% of adults in St. Pierre hold a high school diploma, while only 12% have a bachelor’s degree, reflecting the community’s educational challenges.
